versions.changelog:
- Added developer documentation, including machine contracts and detailed operating/project instructions.
- Introduced new test scripts and expanded golden test data for improved test coverage.
- Removed obsolete or redundant documentation (e.g., skill-card.md).
- Updated core documentation files (README.md, SKILL.md) for clarity and accuracy.
- Adjusted internal tests and build system to support new scripts and documentation structure.

google-health-cli 1.0.8

- Internal changes made to the config handling code (`internal/config/config.go`).
- No user-facing changes in command-line options or behavior.
- All documentation in SKILL.md remains unchanged.

google-health-cli v1.0.7

- Added improved date handling and testing, including new date utilities and tests.
- Introduced hints functionality for CLI usage.
- Enhanced test coverage across CLI and API client components.
- Removed deprecated documentation file (skill-card.md).
- General code maintenance and documentation updates.

- Adds a one-line privacy notice to stderr on all data-emitting commands, reminding users that sensitive health data is printed to stdout.
- Introduces internal/cli/privacy.go to centralize privacy notice handling.
- Updates documentation (README.md, SKILL.md, AGENTS.md) to reflect the new runtime privacy warning.
- Removes the unused skill-card.md file.
- Refactors and tests command logic to ensure all relevant outputs respect the updated privacy messaging.

- Improved privacy and consent guidance in documentation.
- Added a new section on data minimization, end-user consent, and protecting credentials.
- Updated SKILL.md to clarify best practices and responsibilities when handling sensitive health data.
- Removed redundant or outdated documentation files (skill-card.md).
- Minor documentation wording and structural improvements for clarity.

- Added privacy note to documentation: the doctor command now logs local environment metadata such as token-cache/config paths, account info, and API base URL.
- Expanded test coverage with two new test files: source_guards_test.go and testdata_privacy_test.go.
- Updated and clarified documentation and test data to better reflect local environment exposure and privacy implications.
- Internal CLI and test files updated for improved maintainability and accuracy.

**Config and token cache discovery logic improved to be more robust and user-friendly.**

- Token cache location defaults to a non-roaming cache directory; now migrates any previous cache from the old config dir automatically.
- Config file (`config.json`) discovery supports multiple fallback locations for greater flexibility.
- Documentation and metadata updated to clarify new config and token cache lookup order.
- Minor test and code adjustments to support the new cache/config logic.

**Privacy warning added for health data output.**

- SKILL.md now prominently warns that all stdout (from `data list`, `rollup daily`, `sessions`, `api get`) contains sensitive personal health data and may be logged, transmitted, or persisted by downstream tools.
- Clarifies that the tool itself only sends data to Google over HTTPS, but all output is the caller's responsibility.
- Minor doc clarifications; no functional changes to CLI commands or API usage.
- One new test file added; an obsolete doc file removed.

**1.0.1 adds server-side daily roll-up support for Google Health data types.**

- New commands: `rollup daily <type>` fetches per-day reconciled totals, including types not listable via `data list`.
- Documentation updated in README and SKILL.md to cover roll-up concepts, usage, and which types require roll-up.
- Added tests and CLI support for roll-up endpoints.
- No breaking changes to existing commands.

Initial release: Command-line tool to access Google Health data (read-only).

- Authenticate and access your Google Health data via OAuth2; single setup with token auto-refresh.
- List and retrieve raw health data points for all supported Google Health data types (heart rate, sleep, steps, etc.).
- Supports parsed exercise sessions and generic API GET requests.
- Read-only: no write/modify access; only requests read-only API scopes.
- Runs as a self-contained static binary with no external dependencies or runtimes required.
